title: anthocephalus macrophyllus
intro: Anthocephalus macrophyllus, commonly known as Kadam or Neem Gum, is a deciduous tree native to Southeast Asia. The plant is valued for its medicinal properties, which include providing health benefits such as treating fever, diarrhea, and skin conditions due to its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. Its therapeutic actions include antioxidant, anti-diabetic, and anti-cancer activities, attributed to its bioactive constituents which include flavonoids, alkaloids, and terpenoids. These bioactive compounds exhibit anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, contributing to the plant's potential as a natural remedy for various health issues.
